content: Artemisia afra is a widely distributed species of the Artemisia genus found across Africa, ranging from South Africa to regions in the north and east, extending as far as Ethiopia. It is the only indigenous species of Artemisia in Africa. The plant typically grows to a height of 2 to 5 meters. Its leaves are dark green, soft in texture, and resemble the shape of fern leaves. The undersides of the leaves are lighter green and covered with white bristles. Artemisia afra blooms in late summer, producing numerous clusters of butter-colored flowers, each measuring approximately 3 to 5 millimeters in diameter. When any part of the plant is bruised, it releases a strong, sweet, and pungent aroma. Artemisia afra is a well-known medicinal plant in Africa and continues to be effectively used by various cultural groups. Its applications include the treatment of coughs, fevers, colic, headaches, intestinal parasites, and malaria. Additionally, it is commonly employed as a moth repellent and as an ingredient in organic insecticidal sprays. The plant can also be smoked, snuffed, or used in the form of essential oil. Essential oil extracts of Artemisia afra are obtained through steam distillation of its twigs and blossoms.
